name: Lightny Work MVP quality bench
description: Fifteen synthetic, product-level cases covering research, document work, spreadsheets, artifact creation, clarification, revisions, and recovery. No customer data is included.

cases.title: Current OpenAI guidance for evaluating agents
cases.goal: Using only current official OpenAI documentation, identify two practical recommendations for evaluating AI agents. Cite the exact sources beside the relevant claims and keep the answer under 250 words.
human_rubric: Claims are supported by official sources
No process narration replaces the deliverable

cases.title: EU AI Act current implementation summary
cases.goal: Using current official EU sources only, prepare a concise briefing for a small SaaS company on the next two material EU AI Act dates after 16 August 2026 and what each date changes. Cite every date and obligation. Clearly separate facts from practical suggestions.
human_rubric: Briefing is useful to a small company

cases.title: Evidence-linked feedback tools landscape
cases.goal: Research three currently available products that help product teams turn customer feedback into prioritized work. Use each vendor's official product documentation or website, compare evidence linking, collaboration, and export capabilities in a compact table, then identify one underserved angle. Cite every product claim.
human_rubric: Exactly three relevant products are compared
Underserved angle follows from the evidence

cases.title: Product beta decision memo from two files
cases.goal: Read both attached files and write a decision memo for the Atlas beta. Recommend the three highest-priority product changes, explain the evidence for each, name the main risk, and propose one measurable 30-day success criterion. Use only the files and cite the exact filename beside factual claims.
human_rubric: Three priorities follow from the files

cases.title: Contract and policy gap review
cases.goal: Compare the attached vendor contract excerpt with the internal data-handling policy. Produce a table of conflicts or gaps with severity, supporting text, and a negotiation request. Do not use the web and do not provide legal conclusions; label the output as an operational review.

cases.title: Meeting action and decision register
cases.goal: Turn the attached meeting notes into an action register with owner, due date, status, dependency, and source evidence. Do not invent missing owners or dates: mark them as unresolved. Add a separate decisions and open-questions section. Use no web sources.
human_rubric: Decisions and open questions are distinct

cases.title: Sales analysis workbook
cases.goal: Analyze the attached sales CSV and create an Excel workbook with the source data, monthly revenue totals, region totals, and a clear chart of monthly revenue. In the response, summarize the strongest trend and cite the source filename. Do not use the web.

cases.title: Supplier comparison workbook
cases.goal: Compare both attached supplier CSV files and create a polished Excel workbook. Include a normalized comparison table, highlight the lower unit price and faster delivery for each item, preserve payment terms and minimum orders, and add a short recommendation that states any trade-offs. Use only the files and cite the relevant filename beside factual claims.
human_rubric: All rows and terms are preserved

cases.title: Polished one-page beta launch PDF
cases.goal: Using the attached launch brief, create a polished one-page PDF invitation for the Atlas private beta. Preserve every required fact and footer, make the primary action visually clear, avoid unsupported claims, and include a concise inline summary. Do not use the web.
human_rubric: Required footer and action are present

cases.title: Editable action-plan document
cases.goal: Create an editable DOCX action plan from the attached meeting notes. Include an executive summary, action table, decisions, open questions, and a next-review section. Preserve unresolved owners or dates as explicit gaps. Also summarize the result inline. Do not use the web.

cases.title: Ask one material product-launch question
cases.goal: Prepare a launch announcement for our new product. The final wording must be appropriate to the audience and channel, but neither the product nor the audience/channel is provided. Ask one concise question that obtains the minimum information needed before writing the announcement.

interactions.content: It is Atlas, a private beta for operations leads at existing design-partner companies, sent by email. The call to action is to book onboarding.

human_rubric: Only one focused question was asked

cases.title: Proceed without needless clarification
cases.goal: Write a 120-word email invitation for Atlas, a private beta for operations leads at existing design-partner companies. Use a calm, practical tone. The call to action is to book a 30-minute onboarding call. Include the footer 'Private beta. Features and limits may change.' Do not ask follow-up questions and do not use the web.

cases.title: Revise a completed result in conversation
cases.goal: Using the attached product brief, write a decision memo recommending whether Atlas should enter private beta. Include evidence, risks, and a recommendation. Do not use the web.

interactions.content: Revise the memo for a busy founder: keep it under 140 words, preserve the key evidence and risk, and end with a single explicit decision.

cases.title: Turn a prior result into a file
cases.goal: Using the attached meeting notes, produce a concise action register with owners, dates, and unresolved gaps. Do not use the web.

interactions.content: Now turn that action register into a polished editable DOCX with an executive summary and an open-questions section. Keep the same facts and also summarize the file inline.

cases.title: Cancel active research and continue safely
cases.goal: Research current official guidance for evaluating AI agents and prepare a detailed report with citations.

interactions.content: Change direction: do not browse or create files. Give me a five-item forward-looking checklist for planning an internal evaluation, based only on general knowledge.

human_rubric: First run is cancelled rather than completed
Final result is a real five-item checklist
No stale research claim leaks into the result
